title: Mastering Engineering Flow with Windsurf - Eashan Sinha, Windsurf
talk_summary: A Windsurf engineer describes their agentic IDE Cascade, emphasizing 'flow awareness' (tracking user edits, terminal commands, clipboard to infer intent), a hybrid context engine, rules/memories, and deterministic 'workflows' layered over unpredictable agents. The practical advice is to plan with the agent via a checkbox planning file, answer its clarifying questions, and generate/run/fix tests before committing.

takeaways.technique: Checkbox planning file as agent contract
takeaways.what_they_do: Before building, create a planning document with explicit task checkboxes and a stated definition of done, then have the agent work through and check off items while it executes.
takeaways.evidence_quote: create a planning file outline like you know a set of tasks with like maybe checkboxes to tell Cascade hey you need to hit these set of tasks

takeaways.what_they_do: They bridge unpredictable agent behavior with fixed workflow steps so users can define a known sequence the agent must follow.
takeaways.evidence_quote: bridging that gap between the unpredictability of an agent and more of that deterministic nature of a workflow

takeaways.technique: Persistent rules and memories to avoid re-indexing
takeaways.what_they_do: Cascade stores user preferences and codebase memories so it doesn't re-index or re-retrieve the same context every run.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Cascade can generate memories of you as a user, some of your preferences, memories of your codebase so that it doesn't have to constantly index

takeaways.technique: Hybrid context retrieval over pure RAG
takeaways.what_they_do: They combine multiple retrieval tools rather than relying only on embedding search to build explicit codebase context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We don't just use a rag or embedding based search approach. We leverage a combination of multiple tools

takeaways.technique: Agent generates, runs, and fixes tests iteratively
takeaways.what_they_do: In the build phase the agent writes tests, runs them, and fixes failures one by one before the human commits.
takeaways.evidence_quote: generate tests with cascade, right? Um, generate, run, uh, fix your tests one by one as it's iterating
